search_notes: Run one broad-name search for every search_terms_by_agency entry in addition to current and history-handle patterns; results must still pass the include/exclude rules. Search every handle_history handle because riders keep tagging old names after a rename. X date filters are approximate; verify post dates manually before counting. The @tnstc_setc profile self-describes both TNSTC and SETC; its official status is not independently linked from a government site in this audit, so monitor it as a shared candidate handle and flag the uncertainty.
cross_agency_dedupe_rule: When agencies share a handle, search it once. Attribute an incident only when the service/operator is identified; if attribution remains unclear, report it once as a shared/unassigned case and never double-count it across agencies.
include: passenger grievances about a specific service failure: delay, crowding, route/frequency gaps, fare or ticketing problems, staff conduct, safety/accessibility, cleanliness, breakdowns
threads where the rider tags the agency handle (current or legacy) — merge follow-ups into the original incident
exclude: official announcements and scheduler data posted by the agency
national transit stories that do not name a specific failure at the agency
observations that do not establish a specific failure (e.g. 'conductors prefer direct payment' with no incident)
dedupe_rule: One incident = one complaint. Follow-up posts, media add-ons and thread continuations merge into the original post; agency replies never count as complaints.
reply_rule: Any visible reply from the agency handle counts as a reply — but a generic forward, docket number or apology is explicitly NOT a resolution. Every report must label forwarded/acknowledged cases as unresolved.
metrics: approximate response time decoded from post IDs
zero_complaint_check: If a known-active agency returns 0 complaints for the week, treat it as a stale-handle or date-filter smell: verify the handle still resolves (profile loads, recent posts exist) and check legacy handles before writing 'no complaints found'.
limits: X-visible sample only — DMs, deleted posts and encrypted conversations are invisible. An agency reply means any visible response, including a generic forward or docket; it does not imply resolution. Response intervals are approximate, decoded from post IDs. This is not a count of all complaints the agencies receive.
